deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cf. previous and next pages; this is the 1981 'Longue Marche' circle of ideas). Let pi be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, free on the inertia generators l_0 and l_1, with L_i the procyclic subgroup generated by l_i. sigma_infinity is the involution of the S_3-action that swaps l_0 and l_1. Grothendieck studies automorphisms u of pi of the form
- u(l_0) = l_0^p,
- u(l_1) = int(g) l_1^p,
with p = chi(u) in Zhat* (the 'cyclotomic' character) and g in pi.

The question is when the outer class of u commutes with the S_3-action, which is enough to check for sigma_infinity. Concretely, one needs h in pi with u sigma_infinity = int(h) sigma_infinity u. The previous page shows h = g l_1^q, and that the condition is: there exists q with g l_1^q sigma_infinity(g) in L_0.

This page writes that condition as the boxed relation:
  g l_1^q sigma_infinity(g) = l_0^r, for some q, r.
It depends only on g, not on p.

Invariance. Grothendieck checks that (q, r) is unchanged under the substitution g -> g' = l_0^alpha g l_1^{-alpha}, which comes from changing the representative of the outer class in the normalizer of L_0. Since sigma_infinity(g') = l_1^alpha sigma_infinity(g) l_0^{-alpha}, the l_1 exponents cancel and the relation for g' is the l_0^alpha-conjugate of the relation for g. Uniqueness of (q, r) given g also holds, because in a free profinite group a power of l_1 cannot be conjugate to a nontrivial power of l_0.

Example. For tau (complex conjugation), p = -1 and g = l_1. The relation reads l_1^{1+q} l_0 = l_0^r, so q = -1 and r = 1.

Discrete case. He recalls that for the discrete free group, the only solutions besides the identity require p = ±1 and that l_0^p and int(g) l_1^p generate pi. The only nontrivial solution is tau.

Margin. He proposes rewriting the relation as sigma_infinity(g^{±1}) = l_0^beta g l_1^gamma, notes that q = -r, and after renormalizing g gets sigma_infinity(g') = l_0^beta g l_1^beta.

The next page packages this into invariants on Gamma = Autext_loc(pi_{0,3}, S_3):
- gamma: Gamma -> pi/Zhat, with Zhat acting by phi(alpha).g = l_0^alpha g l_1^{-alpha};
- chi: Gamma -> Zhat*.
He asserts that (gamma, chi) is injective.

Modern reading. With f = g^{-1}, x = l_0, y = l_1, this is the Ihara/Drinfeld parametrization sigma -> (lambda, f_sigma). The boxed relation is the non-normalized form of Drinfeld's relation (I), f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1. Abelianizing shows q = -r is forced; normalizing f into the closure of the commutator subgroup gives q = r = 0, i.e. exactly relation (I). The injectivity of (gamma, chi) is the injectivity of Gamma (and of Gal(Qbar/Q), via Belyi) into pairs (lambda, f).
errors: The quantifier 'q, r in Zhat*' should be 'q, r in Zhat'. The previous page has q in Zhat, and the normalized solution is q = r = 0, which is not a unit.

Gap: g is only determined by u up to right multiplication by L_1 (u(l_1) = g l_1^p g^{-1}), and changing the representative by int(l_0^alpha) multiplies g on the left by l_0^alpha. The full ambiguity is therefore g -> l_0^alpha g l_1^beta with alpha and beta independent. Under g -> g l_1^beta one finds (q, r) -> (q - beta, r + beta). The page checks invariance only for the diagonal family l_0^alpha g l_1^{-alpha}. So 'q, r depend only on the outer action' is not justified unless g has been normalized. The margin ('i.e. q = -r', renormalizing g) and the next page (gamma with values in pi/phi(Zhat)) suggest Grothendieck noticed this and repaired it by normalization.
The fact that q = -r is automatic (by abelianization: if g ≡ l_0^a l_1^b, then r = a + b = -q) is not stated in the main text, only in the margin.

ideas.what: Parametrize outer automorphisms of pi_{0,3}-hat preserving inertia by (p, g) with u(l_0) = l_0^p, u(l_1) = g l_1^p g^{-1}; the pair (chi, class of g) is injective
ideas.modern_name: Ihara-Drinfeld parametrization sigma -> (chi(sigma), f_sigma); injectivity of GT-hat into Zhat* x F2-hat
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in outline

ideas.what: Compatibility with the S_3-involution sigma_infinity expressed as g l_1^q sigma_infinity(g) = l_0^r
ideas.modern_name: GT relation (I): f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 (2-cycle relation), in non-normalized form
ideas.where_published: probably in the Longue Marche manuscript material (1981); not in Esquisse in this explicit form

ideas.what: Ambiguity g -> l_0^alpha g l_1^{-alpha} and the invariant gamma with values in pi/Zhat
ideas.modern_name: Choice of normalization of f_sigma (Drinfeld fixes it by f in the closure of the commutator subgroup)

ideas.what: Discrete case: Out(F_2) elements of this type are only the identity and complex conjugation tau

missed.claim: This is an explicit 1981 derivation of the 2-cycle relation of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group from commutation with the S_3-symmetry, nine years before Drinfeld's GT-hat. Grothendieck uses a non-normalized cocycle g with invariants (q, r); this normalization differs from Drinfeld's but is equivalent. Historically documentary rather than mathematically new: the relation itself is now standard.
missed.quote: ∃ q,r ... tels que g l_1^q σ_∞(g) = l_0^r (condition qui ne dépend que de g, pas de p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents precisely how far Grothendieck had gone toward GT-hat in 1981 (relation I and the injectivity of (gamma, chi)), relevant to the attribution of the 'Grothendieck-Teichmüller' group.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is essentially Drinfeld/Ihara relation (I) and the (lambda, f) parametrization, which are well known. Grothendieck's 1981 work on the Galois action on pi_{0,3} is known through La Longue Marche, but this explicit computation is a moderately interesting archival confirmation of priority on relation (I). It contains a small normalization gap, which he himself seems to have patched in the margin.
transcription_corrections: 'q, r ∈ Ẑ*': mathematically this should be Ẑ (the previous page has q ∈ Ẑ); the asterisk is either a slip by Grothendieck or a misreading.
'il n'y a qu'une seule autre relation de nos équations' should read 'il n'y a qu'une seule autre solution de nos équations'.

Margin likely reads: 'il vaut mieux écrire la relation sous la forme σ_∞(g^{-1}) = l_0^β g l_1^γ ; on trouve, si on change g en g' (convenable), (i.e. q=-r) β=γ, donc σ_∞(g'^{-1}) = l_0^β g l_1^β' (exponent on g partly illegible).
'en exigeant {+donc p=±1 et+} que l_0^p et int(g) l_1^p engendrent π' is correct; the crossed-out word before 'engendrent' is a false start of the same word.
